steps.what: Check actual meat inventories, usable condition and expected waste
Assemble recorded meat usage and inventory quantities for replenishment
Estimate meat requirements using demand, yield and supply constraints
Prepare the complete meat order or requisition with delivery and price details
Check the final meat supplies order against the actual purchasing authority
Submit the exact authorised meat supplies order to the supplier

tasks.design: Use existing stock and usage records in {OPS_SYSTEM} to generate the replenishment comparison currently assembled in {SPREADSHEET}. The butcher judges usable stock and requirements, completes a native {PROCUREMENT} order and submits only the exact order checked by the actual purchasing manager.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recorded stock and sales are manually assembled before quantities and supplier fields are re-entered.
tasks.enabler_now: Native usage views and catalogue forms remove fixed compilation and repeated order fields.
tasks.still_hard: Yield, freshness, demand changes and supplier substitutions require practical judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Order usable meat in the right quantities without relying on book stock alone.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: stock and usage comparisons can be generated from existing records, while usable-stock assessment and meat replenishment judgement remain human.

assumptions: OTHER means physical stock and weighing tools. Boundary is the actual replenishment order in a setting with an existing purchasing manager, not receipt or payment.

Till operators and goods-movement staff create existing item, quantity, unit and date records in their ordinary transactions. s1 counts the butcher's physical verification; its corrections feed s2. Missing or incompatible usage rows require funded manual repair.

s2 replaces actual manual compilation only where a native usage view is not already used. s4 removes seven units of repeated supplier, item and delivery fields, retaining13 for chosen quantities, price and substitutions.

s5 is the actual purchasing mandate check after the complete order exists, not author self-approval of notes. The send binds that exact supplier, item, quantity, price and delivery snapshot; changes void it. The current tiny submission and ordinary ungated draft save earn no saving.
research_questions: Can stock corrections and supplier units be reconciled before quantities are proposed?

tasks.short: Record received and issued meat quantities

steps.what: Weigh the actual meat received or issued and compare it with the movement document
outputs: verified movement weight and discrepancy observations

steps.what: Capture meat item, lot, supplier or destination and actual movement quantity
inputs: verified movement weight and discrepancy observations

steps.what: Copy the checked meat movement fields into the receiving or issue register draft
Check the meat register against the actual movement and correct discrepancies
Save the meat received or issued record in its existing register

tasks.design: Link checked scale or receipt fields from the meat workstation {OTHER} into the actual stock register {OPS_SYSTEM}, replacing the manual bridge through {SPREADSHEET}. The butcher still measures the real movement, captures missing traceability facts and checks the assembled record before an ordinary save.
tasks.previous_blocker: Already captured weight and delivery fields are copied into a separate register.
tasks.enabler_now: Native scale exports and field mappings can remove the actual second entry without a model.
tasks.still_hard: A supplier label may not match the meat actually received, and issue destinations must be factual.
tasks.human_edge: Catch weight, lot and destination discrepancies at the physical movement.

ambition.what: The butcher remains responsible for factual movement records.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: scale and delivery fields can feed a meat movement register deterministically, replacing manual copying while actual receipt and traceability checks remain human.

assumptions: OTHER means the existing scale and goods-movement capture tool. Boundary is one actual received-or-issued movement record, not both pre-delivery and post-delivery phases in one entry.

The supplier supplies delivery and lot details; the butcher verifies the physical movement in s1 and captures item, lot, supplier or destination, quantity, unit and date in s2. No new capture is presumed free and planned quantities do not prove actual movement.

s3 replaces actual manual copying from the workstation or delivery fields through the paper or spreadsheet bridge described in the digest. Native import is tried first; already automatic till or scale recording earns no additional labour benefit.

Unreadable labels and unit or item mismatches stop for funded manual repair. The integration creates draft register fields, not a purchase or financial release. The final ordinary author save is tiny, fully retained and ungated; no self-approval is added.
research_questions: Can each saved quantity retain the actual lot and source movement reference?

already_counted.description: Measure the movement, capture source facts, check the register and save

incremental.description: Maintain scale and register mappings and manually repair unreadable or incompatible movement fields

steps.what: Read the current production plan before supervising meat cutters
Write the actual work allocation for other butchers and meat cutters
Explain the meat cutters' work allocation and check their understanding
Supervise other butchers through direct observation, correction and coaching

tasks.design: Open current production priorities directly in {OPS_SYSTEM} and reuse the existing work-allocation format in {DOCS}. The supervising butcher chooses assignments, explains them and observes cutting directly; no staff ranking or automated competence allocation is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the current plan and recreating the work sheet surround direct supervision.
tasks.enabler_now: Native production views and a reusable assignment layout reduce navigation and headings.
tasks.still_hard: Safe cutting technique, hygiene and changing workload need direct observation.
tasks.human_edge: Correct unsafe work immediately and coach the individual cutter.

ambition.what: Supervision and assignment decisions remain with the butcher.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: existing production views and work-sheet formats can reduce clerical supervision preparation while direct cutting supervision remains human.

assumptions: OTHER means the cutting room and ordinary face-to-face instruction. Boundary includes the current work allocation actually used to coordinate the team, not a new staff-performance or end-of-shift report.

Production planners maintain current requirements; the supervising butcher reads them in s1 and creates the actual allocation in s2 from current staff knowledge. No new staff monitoring or free competence database is assumed.

s1 removes one unit of plan navigation. s2 removes three units of repeated work-sheet headings, retaining12 for actual allocation and checks. The spoken explanation and physical supervision retain all75 units.
Ordinary author save within the existing work sheet is negligible, retained and ungated. The sheet is working coordination, not a formal staffing commitment requiring invented author approval.
unknowns: Whether the team uses a written allocation today
research_questions: Does the existing work sheet repeat structure that can be reused without changing assignment judgement?

already_counted.description: Read priorities, write actual allocations, explain them and supervise cutting

incremental.description: Maintain the production link and allocation format

steps.what: Read current supply-company terms and the order details needing negotiation
Negotiate order details with supply-company representatives within the actual mandate
Write the negotiated order details and unresolved conditions for the actual buyer
Save the proposed order details in the existing purchasing file

tasks.design: Keep the actual supplier terms directly accessible in {PROCUREMENT} and use a concise order-detail format in {DOCS}. The butcher negotiates price, cut specification, quantity and delivery conditions personally and records the proposed terms used by the buyer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Current terms are found across files and repeated supplier fields are written into negotiation notes.
tasks.enabler_now: Native supplier views and a terms format shorten lookup and repeated entry.
tasks.still_hard: Supplier flexibility, quality and delivery tradeoffs emerge during the conversation.
tasks.human_edge: Judge the offer and preserve a workable supplier relationship.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: supplier-term views and structured negotiation notes can reduce lookup and repeated fields while supplier negotiation remains human.

assumptions: Boundary is the actual negotiation and its proposed terms used in purchasing, not a binding order, contract signature or supplier confirmation. The butcher works within the actual nonbinding negotiation mandate; order authorisation and send are separate replenishment work.

Purchasing maintains current supplier terms. The butcher reads actual requirements and mandate in s1 and captures actual proposals in s3 after the call; no model invents a discount or delivery promise.

s1 removes three units of searching current terms, retaining12 for reading. s3 removes1.4 units of repeated supplier and order headers, retaining12.6 for actual negotiated detail and checks. The70 conversation units remain fully retained.

The notes are the real order-detail input read by the buyer, not an invented trailing report. The one-unit ordinary save remains fully retained and ungated. Native access already present earns no additional benefit.
research_questions: Can the record distinguish proposed conditions from a formally accepted order?

already_counted.description: Read current terms, negotiate, write actual proposed details and save

incremental.description: Maintain supplier-term links and the order-detail format
